name: Rehum
overview: The name Rehum appears in Scripture referring to several individuals connected to the post-exilic period of Israel’s history. One Rehum was a chancellor who, alongside Shimshai the scribe, actively opposed the rebuilding efforts in Jerusalem by writing letters to King Artaxerxes, which ultimately led to the cessation of the Jews' work by force (Ezra 4:8-9, 17, 23). Another Rehum was a Levite who faithfully repaired a section of Jerusalem’s wall, demonstrating dedication to the restoration of the city and worship (Nehemiah 3:17). Additionally, Rehum is listed among the captives who returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel, highlighting his role in the community’s return and covenant renewal (Ezra 2:2). These references collectively portray Rehum as both an adversary to and a supporter of God's people during a critical time of rebuilding and spiritual renewal.
